properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's North-blocks pass: real OSM building footprint. Edgewater, 355 Berry St -- rental apartment building on Mission Creek. EXTENDED 2026-09-20 per owner review of the numbered real-gap-fragment technique (used this session for P8/P2): the owner pointed at fragment 10 (computed as bbox.difference(streets).difference(tracked polygons) over the Edgewater/freeway-curve area, ~6,836 sqm) as the real extent of N4-3's own open-land strip alongside I-280, separate from the Edgewater building itself but sharing its N4-3 label. Split that fragment using two lines the owner specified directly: Mission Walk 330's own southwest edge (S-W corner) and northeast edge (N-E corner), each extended as a full line through the fragment. The resulting southern, triangular piece (~4,704 sqm, tapering along the freeway curve) is this record's N4-3 extension; the piece north of the northeast line went to Mission Walk 330 instead (see that record); a small remainder beyond both cuts was dropped per the owner's instruction. Result is a MultiPolygon: Edgewater's own building footprint plus this separate open-land strip, which doesn't touch the building directly (a real planted buffer runs between them). REVERTED 2026-09-20: the 'N4-3 open-land strip' added above was wrong -- checking it against DataSF Assessor parcels found it overlaps 96.7% with a real, distinct parcel (blklot 8704004, 360 Berry St -- 'Mission Bay by Windsor'), not open land. The owner separately corrected the 2026-09-19 finding that Windsor and Edgewater are the same building (a 99.6% footprint-overlap check that was apparently comparing the wrong candidate geometry) -- they are two separate condo complexes on separate parcels (355 Berry St vs 360 Berry St). Reverted this record to just its own real OSM footprint; Windsor is now tracked separately (status.csv blklot 8704004).
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be joined via status.csv the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same pattern already used for Mission Bay's other condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon I/II/III, Madrone, Arden, One Mission Bay, Radiance).
